subject: Accounting
title: Payroll Bookkeeping
description: A quick, practical guide to Payroll Bookkeeping.

hook.text: An employee earns $5,000 but takes home $3,800. The rest? Taxes, insurance, and retirement.

buildup.text: Payroll bookkeeping records gross wages, withholdings, employer taxes, and net pay for every employee.

discovery.text: It creates liabilities for taxes owed to the government and benefits owed to providers.

twist.text: Payroll errors are among the most common bookkeeping mistakes—and the most costly in penalties.

climax.text: Accurate payroll protects employees, satisfies the IRS, and keeps the business out of legal trouble.

punchline.text: Payroll has zero room for error. Get it right every time.

quiz.question: What does payroll bookkeeping track?
options: Gross wages, withholdings, employer taxes, and net pay
Just the company's total labor cost

details.summary: Payroll bookkeeping records employee compensation, tax withholdings, benefits deductions, and employer tax obligations. This topic explains the journal entries involved and why payroll is one of the most complex recurring bookkeeping tasks.
details.whyItMatters: Payroll errors affect employees directly and can trigger penalties from tax authorities. Accurate payroll bookkeeping is both a legal obligation and a trust issue with your team.
takeaways: Payroll entries must account for gross pay, employee withholdings, and employer-paid taxes
Employer payroll taxes like Social Security and Medicare are separate expenses from wages
Payroll tax deposits have strict deadlines with significant penalties for late payment

faq.question: What makes payroll bookkeeping so complex?
faq.answer: Payroll involves multiple accounts per employee: gross wages, federal and state income tax withholdings, Social Security and Medicare taxes (both employee and employer portions), benefits deductions, and net pay. Each component has different regulatory requirements.

faq.question: What happens if payroll taxes are paid late?
faq.answer: The IRS imposes escalating penalties for late payroll tax deposits: 2% for deposits 1-5 days late, up to 15% for amounts still unpaid 10 days after a final notice. In severe cases, the responsible person can be held personally liable for unpaid payroll taxes.
